title: Finite chart and relation fibres make every field representative quasi-compact
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and $x\in|X|$ a field-valued point class [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Suppose $(a_i:U_i\to X)_{i\in I}$ is a set-indexed jointly surjective family of representable etale morphisms from schemes [def-weil-etale-morphism], meaning that the union of the images of $|U_i|\to|X|$ is $|X|$. Put $R_i=U_i\times_XU_i$ with first projection $p_i:R_i\to U_i$, using sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Assume that for every $i\in I$ the sets $|a_i|^{-1}(\{x\})$ and $|a_i p_i|^{-1}(\{x\})$ are finite. Then every $S$-morphism $u:\operatorname{Spec}L\to X$ from a field $L$ [def-weil-field, def-weil-affine-spectrum] representing $x$ is quasi-compact: for every affine scheme $T\to X$ the scheme $T\times_X\operatorname{Spec}L$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. No quasi-separatedness, finite-type or Noetherian assumption is imposed on $X$ or the $U_i$, and the individual fibres may be empty.

source.place: Tag 03JV (lemma-UR-finite-above-x), implication (2) to (6); the lemma allows schemes U_i without affineness or quasi-compactness.

proof.text: Apply change of base to $S\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, writing $X^{\mathrm{abs}}=j_!X$. Its etale scheme charts and their fibre products are the same schemes. Its field-valued representatives are pairs consisting of an $S$-structure and a representative in $X$; equality after a common field extension is exactly equality of those pairs. Thus its point classes, chart fibres and relation fibres identify with those in the hypothesis. We may prove quasi-compactness for the corresponding absolute field morphism: every original affine $S$-scheme test is also an absolute affine test, and its fibre product is unchanged. Work with this absolute space in the following steps.

source.place: Tags 03I4 (lemma-change-base-scheme) and 04SG (lemma-category-of-spaces-over-smaller-base-scheme), applied to the base of Tag 03JV.

proof.text: Apply finite-fibre transfer to the given covering $(U_i\to X)_i$. For every affine representable etale chart $V\to X$ the set $F_V=\{v\in|V|:v\mapsto x\}$ is finite. This application uses only the chart-fibre hypothesis, and imposes no quasi-compactness on $U_i$.

source.place: Tag 03JV (lemma-UR-finite-above-x), (2) to (1), first sentence, using Tag 03JS.

proof.text: Joint surjectivity supplies $i$ and $u\in U_i$ over $x$. The set of $r\in R_i$ with both projections equal to $u$ is a subset of the assumed finite fibre of $|R_i|\to|X|$ at $x$, so is finite. Apply the residual-relation lemma with $U=U_i$: for $K=\kappa(u)$ and $b:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$, both projections of $\operatorname{Spec}K\times_X\operatorname{Spec}K$ are etale and quasi-compact. The existing self-relation lemma therefore gives a field $k$ and a monomorphism $j:\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ in the class $x$. Only this one chart must have a nonempty fibre.

source.place: Tag 03JV (lemma-UR-finite-above-x), (2) to (1), applying Tag 03JU to one chart meeting x.

proof.text: Fix any affine representable etale chart $V\to X$ and set $D=V\times_X\operatorname{Spec}k$. Base change of the etale chart makes $D\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ etale. The projection $D\to V$ is a monomorphism: two maps with equal $V$-coordinates have equal field coordinates by monomorphy of $j$, hence coincide by the fibre-product property. In particular it is injective on maps from field spectra. The field-point equivalence in the radicial node implies it is universally injective, hence injective on underlying points. Its image lies in $F_V$, since its composite to $X$ has class $x$ at every point. Thus $|D|$ is finite by step 2.

source.place: Tag 03JV (lemma-UR-finite-above-x), obtaining condition (3); Tag 01S4 (lemma-universally-injective), field-point criterion.

proof.text: Apply the etale-fibre decomposition to $D\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ at its unique point; this fibre is $D$ itself. It is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable extensions $k_d/k$, indexed by $d\in|D|$. Step 4 makes that index set finite. The component open immersions of the finite-product-spectrum lemma identify the disjoint union with $\operatorname{Spec}(\prod_d k_d)$, so $D=\operatorname{Spec}(\prod_d k_d)$ and the coordinate algebra is a finite-dimensional $k$-module: concatenate a finite basis of each factor. By the definition of a finite morphism, $D\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is finite; the empty case has zero coordinate algebra and also satisfies this assertion. We have verified this for every affine etale chart, so apply the existing finite-chart criterion to $j$. It gives quasi-compactness of every field representative of $x$, on every affine test $T\to X$, with no etale restriction on $T$. Step 1 identifies these fibre products with the original $S$-fibre products and proves the assertion.
